Article.ArticleTitle: Colonoscopy-based Clostridioides difficile screening for inflammatory bowel disease patients.

Article.ArticleTitle: Interpretable machine learning applied to high-dimensional salivary proteomics in pediatric inflammatory bowel diseases.

Abstract.AbstractText: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBDs), including Crohn's disease (CD), ulcerative colitis (UC), and inflammatory bowel disease unclassified (IBD-U), are chronic inflammatory disorders of the gastrointestinal tract. Current methods for classification and longitudinal monitoring are invasive, expensive, and often delayed, limiting timely diagnosis and management. This proof-of-concept study reports the

Unstimulated saliva from pediatric CD, UC, and IBD-U patients was analyzed using Alamar Biosciences' NULISAseq 250 Protein Inflammation Panel. Logistic regression with recursive feature elimination identified a candidate minimal discriminative signature. Performance was further assessed using follow-up samples. Differential abundance analysis between UC and CD revealed 53 significantly different proteins. ML identified a 14-protein signature comprising chemokines/cytokines (CCL1, IFNA1-IFNA13, IL12p70, IL34, TNFSF11/RANKL), receptors/ligands (CD40LG, ICOSLG, IL1R2, IL17RA), structural/tissue-remodeling proteins (CD93, GFAP, SPP1), and growth factors/immune modulators (GDF2, GZMA). This first-in-field integration of salivary proteomics with interpretable artificial intelligence/ML demonstrates that accurate, noninvasive classification of pediatric IBD is possible using minimal biomarker sets.
